interaction.user_prompt: Issue #15: add a file-operation queue with progress/ETA/speed indicator (branch 15-file-operations-progress-indicator-2)
interaction.model_cot:
Context Summary:
Repo is at main + "Update CLAUDE.md". An earlier, never-merged attempt exists on origin/15-file-operations-progress-indicator (commits 4526ee4, b2ce5b4, 8a4a55b, 585dbdb, +443/-41 across commands.go, fs.go, model.go, msg.go, styles.go, update.go, view.go). The "-2" branch is a fresh restart from main, so that work is NOT in the current tree.</context_summary>
<parameter name="reasoning">Reviewed the abandoned attempt via `git diff main...origin/15-file-operations-progress-indicator` rather than starting blind. It is a useful negative result — reasons I am NOT cherry-picking it:

1. Unbuffered `progressChan` + a blocking `progressChan <- msg` on every 32KB chunk. The copy goroutine stalls until the Bubble Tea event loop drains each message, so disk I/O is throttled to UI framerate. This is the central design flaw.
2. Only one `waitForProgressMsg` is armed at a time, but `copyStartedMsg` arms a new reader per operation, so with N concurrent ops the reader count drifts. On the `allDone` branch it returns without re-arming, leaving a reader blocked on the channel forever — it then eats the first message of the *next* operation.
3. `tea.Sequence(operationCmd, m.processOverwriteConflicts())` is broken once the op is async: operationCmd returns `copyStartedMsg` immediately after spawning the goroutine, so Sequence no longer serializes the overwrite loop against actual completion.
4. `ProgressState.StartTime` is one timestamp for the whole batch, so "speed" is a lifetime average, not current throughput. No ETA at all, which the issue explicitly asks for.
5. No queue and no management: it keeps a `map[int]OpProgress` of concurrently-running ops with no ordering, no cancel, and no way to inspect them.

Also found a PRE-EXISTING bug in main (not introduced by that branch): in `copyFilesCmd`/`moveFilesCmd`, if *any* source file conflicts, the command returns `fileConflictMsg` and copies nothing; the y/n/A/s loop in `Update` then only ever operates on the conflicting files. Non-conflicting files in the same selection are silently dropped.

Chosen direction instead: serial queue of operations; workers publish progress into atomic counters owned by the op; a ~100ms `tea.Tick` polls those counters, computes EWMA-smoothed speed and ETA in `Update`, starts the next queued op, and stops ticking when idle. No progress channel at all, so no throttling and no deadlock. Conflict resolution moves to enqueue time (probe -> resolve -> enqueue one op with an approved file list), which both decouples the modal flow from execution and fixes the dropped-files bug.</reasoning>
<parameter name="response">Analysis complete; about to confirm scope (delete in queue? serial vs parallel? fix adjacent bugs?) with the user before implementing.
